subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should credential-shaped keys explicitly configured in `skills.entries.<skill>.env` bypass the generic sensitive-name block for that active skill's host run while dangerous host override names remain blocked?
rationale: The source and docs support the regression, but the repair changes a credential-to-exec boundary and must be reconciled with the open inverse secret-leak issue.

options.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
options.body: Permit keys explicitly present in the active skill config to pass the sensitive-name check, with tests for dangerous-name rejection, gog-like credential delivery, and unrelated exec isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare each sensitive env name in metadata, then update docs or doctor guidance so users do not expect arbitrary credential-shaped `env` keys to work.

options.title: Defer to a credential contract
options.body: Pause this bypass until maintainers define a broader SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit keys explicitly present in the active skill config to pass the sensitive-name check, with tests for dangerous-name rejection, gog-like credential delivery, and unrelated exec isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent merged history in the overlapping skill env and SecretRef repair path.
